comparator.name: Theologie
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 OER, established on 9 July 2026 and effective from 1 September 2026, defines a three-year, 180-EC Dutch bachelor in Utrecht. Year 1 is a fixed 60-EC theological foundation. Year 2 combines one 24-EC disciplinary track, Greek (15 EC), Hebrew (15 EC) and 6 EC of personal development and worldview; the OER also permits a no-language replacement pathway, but that is an alternative rather than the primary formal table used here. Year 3 consists of a 30-EC minor, 9 EC in exegesis and source languages, a 6-EC theology/media/current-affairs component and a 15-EC final project. The generic registry target names no track. All four tracks carry the same formal weight, so Systematische Theologie, the first track in the OER's official list, is selected by a neutral source-order tie-break fixed independently of UCR fit. The current target and official sources specify the Utrecht programme; registry interest evidence still points to an older Groningen partnership page, so those stale Groningen-specific interests do not override the authoritative Utrecht curriculum. The selected primary language pathway remains unchanged. It must not be generalized to every bachelor route: the explicit language-free option replaces Greek/Hebrew 30 EC with four additional track courses (24 EC) and Interreligieuze praktijken (6 EC), and replaces source-language exegesis 9 EC with a previously untaken track course (6 EC) and Recente eigen theologische publicatie (3 EC). Languages and exegesis are required for the predikantsmaster exit profile, rather than universally for all bachelor students. These mutually exclusive replacements are not added to the selected 180-EC route. The current adopted OER was rechecked on 2026-10-08; the UCR assessment retains its original date and evidence.

routeSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic Utrecht bachelor Theologie and names no disciplinary track. The 2026-2027 OER requires 24 EC in one of four tracks—Systematische Theologie, Historische Theologie, Praktische Theologie or Bijbelwetenschappen—and gives them equal formal weight. No source identifies a default or broader track. The neutral official-order tie-break therefore selects Systematische Theologie, the first listed track, before UCR fit is considered. The main Greek-and-Hebrew pathway in the formal curriculum table is retained; the OER's no-language option is an explicit replacement route rather than the selected primary pathway.

alternatives.label: Worldviews, cultural traditions & public life
alternatives.concept: Study questions of belief, meaning and the good life through philosophy, myth, literature, archaeology and visual heritage, then examine religious diversity, rights, institutions and conflict through sociology, psychology, law and politics. This is a related-fields programme, not a substitute for Christian theology, biblical languages, exegesis or pastoral formation.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines philosophy and cultural interpretation with law, sociology, politics and psychology. The label names those related fields and does not imply a Theology degree.
progression: Introductory philosophy, sociology, politics, archaeology and law precede advanced constitutional, social-theory, conflict, heritage and interpretive work. Law, Society & Justice precedes Comparative Constitutional Law. All courses use exact planned terms; seven are at 300 level.

candidates.label: Biblical languages, exegesis & ancient religious texts
candidates.assessment: The current Utrecht curriculum independently confirms biblical studies, Greek, Hebrew and source-language exegesis, but UCR offers no Greek or Hebrew sequence, scriptural exegesis, biblical-studies progression or theology research environment. General courses on myth, antiquity and cultural history are already bounded contributions to the first programme and cannot sustain this direction.

candidates.label: Practical theology, ministry & spiritual care
candidates.assessment: The older Groningen-specific trajectory in row 6693 is no longer the current target structure, while the current Utrecht page independently confirms practical theology and preparation for the predikantsmaster. UCR can study care, institutions and psychology, but it has no theology, pastoral formation, supervised spiritual-care practice or ministry curriculum.

selection.assessment: The historical judgment correctly identified the absence of Christian theology, biblical languages, exegesis and pastoral formation, but applied a full-substitution threshold. One coherent related-fields programme is defensible in worldviews, cultural traditions and public life. Biblical-language/exegesis and ministry/spiritual-care directions remain infeasible, so production stops at one. The current Utrecht programme and 2026-2027 OER control; stale Groningen-specific details do not alter the target.

blocks: Both support personal reflection and formation; UCR PPD is general and not theological or spiritual formation.
The comparator requires an independent theology final project; UCR optional research is shown separately and does not supply theology-specific supervision or methods.

notes.text: PThU Theologie is a Protestant Christian-theology degree with systematic, historical, practical and biblical theology, Greek and Hebrew, source-language exegesis, personal worldview formation and an independent theology final project. UCR can study worldviews, meaning, cultural traditions and religion in public life through adjacent humanities and social sciences, but the UCR route does not reproduce the theological discipline.

UCR offers no biblical Greek or Hebrew, sustained scriptural exegesis, systematic or pastoral theology, Reformation theology, ministry preparation or supervised spiritual-care practice. Philosophy, literature, heritage, law and sociology remain related perspectives rather than substitutes for those components.
